title: Choose the dashboard layout
question: Same Blue Book look (navy ink, one blue, ruled, no cards). Pick how the dashboard is arranged on a laptop; it stacks on a phone either way.

options.label: Money Flow
options.lineage: Sankey flow diagrams of public budgets
options.thesis: Show where the money comes from and where it goes in one picture: property tax and other funding flowing into each budget section.
options.viewport: Headline numbers strip across the top; a full-width flow chart (levy and other funding → 12 sections); under it, departments requested-vs-proposed and biggest changes side by side; receipt lookup in the right column.
options.risk: Flow charts are striking but take a moment to read; needs clear labels and a table toggle.

options.label: Front-Page Broadsheet
options.lineage: newspaper front pages and sports-page box scores
options.thesis: Lay it out like a front page: one big lead chart, a box score of the key numbers beside it, and departments as a standings table.
options.viewport: Title and one-line summary; lead treemap of the budget by section (two-thirds width) with a box score column (all funds, general city, levy, rate) beside it; below, revenue bars, departments standings, and biggest movers in three columns.
options.risk: Dense on a laptop if every column is full; needs generous rules and whitespace.

options.label: Your Receipt First
options.thesis: Lead with the resident's own question: type an address and the dashboard below shows your share of each part of the budget.
options.viewport: Big address lookup across the top with the levy-vs-rate explainer; below, a two-column grid: where your city tax goes (personalised after lookup, citywide before), where the money comes from, departments, biggest changes.
options.risk: Journalists and visitors who don't want to type an address see a quieter first screen.
